chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan and Fadalah from al-Ala' said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I shaved my head and sacrificed (the animal) while I was in the state of Tamattu'. Can I anoint my head with henna?' He said: 'Yes, provided you do not touch any of the perfume.' I said: 'And I wear the qamis (seamless garment) and cover my head (with the qamis)?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Before I perform Tawaf around the House?' He said: 'Yes.'

key_terms.اَلْقَمِيصَ: A seamless garment worn over the ihram
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعٌ: A pilgrim who performs Umrah first, then Hajj, keeping the ihram between the two

ai.seo_question: What are the permissible acts for a Mu'tamir after shaving his head during Hajj al-Tamattu?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the transitional state of the Mu'tamir after shaving but before the final Tawaf, specifically addressing the permissibility of wearing the qamis and covering the head (taqannu') while maintaining the prohibition of perfume (tayyib). It highlights the scholarly distinction between general clothing and the specific restrictions of Ihram, reinforcing the practical application of ritual purity in Hajj jurisprudence.
